PullRequest.Title: agentHost: expand shell and Codex persistence E2E coverage
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
- Add native Copilot shell compaction recovery, Codex image restoration after restart, and invalid-skill diagnostics E2E coverage.
- Strengthen worktree subscriber reconciliation and directory/branch metadata assertions.
- Normalize generated shell-output paths, canonicalize text-only replay content, and cover both with harness tests.
- Compare skill paths by file identity and remove watched workspaces after the shared Codex process exits.

Tests/harness/docs only. Existing provider/platform gates unchanged. No fail-before/pass-after product regression proof is claimed.

## Current validation
Merged origin/main; current head `9c9b8423c8197583c6e3c682512fa9828e861dae`, Copilot1.0.84-5, Codex0.153.0.
- Reproduced and fixed review finding3991083094. Generated bindings expand before username/home/workspace placeholders; thread resolved.
- 21 harness unit tests, 5 focused E2Es, full deterministic E2E suite, typecheck, ESLint and hygiene passed.
- [Code OSS](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/35036038037) passed first attempt.
- Packaged Electron integration steps passed twice in [474147](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=474147) and [474148](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=474148). Exact added/strengthened test results and teardown verified in all six logs.
- Actual packaged test architectures: Windows x64, Linux x64, macOS arm64 (current pipeline target). Existing Windows/Codex worktree gates unchanged.
- Both packaged builds474147 and474148 are fully green. All merged-head validation is complete; human review approval remains.

## Historical notes
Previous head also passed two full packaged builds. Earlier pre-existing Copilot subagent/file-denial flakes were not hidden by weaker assertions. Coverage files retain the earlier successful aggregate measurement.

(Written by Copilot)

Scenarios.Scenario: Record and replay model exchanges with generated UUID and compacted-shell-output placeholders
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On recording shutdown, captured exchanges are projected, traversed for shell-output paths and UUIDs, serialized to YAML, and written. On each replayed model request, placeholder values are captured and the request is normalized before comparison; replay cannot respond until this local work completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and parse a YAML fixture on construction/reset
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fixture read and parse occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before replay requests can be served

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and write the recorded YAML fixture
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once when a recording proxy stops
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same YAML serialization and single write occurred; the diff adds an in-memory shell-path normalization traversal before it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serve model requests through the loopback replay HTTP server
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One loopback request per recorded model exchange
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same loopback model exchange occurred; matching previously normalized only UUID bindings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Request projection and placeholder normalization complete before the replay response

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixture exchange count, request-history bytes, and generated placeholders in the current fixture. resetForReplay clears the placeholder map, so effective cardinality is bounded to one test fixture; the new captures contain at most a few exchanges and placeholders.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single in-process HTTP proxy handles each model request; fixture writing and request comparison are synchronous and uncoalesced, but each test fixture is processed independently and serially.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fixtures are parsed from disk when loaded/reset; there is no normalization cache. Placeholder bindings are warm within a test and cleared between tests. The diff adds one shell-path traversal at write time and one escaped-value replacement per bound placeholder, but realistic fixtures have small bounded cardinality.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added traversals and scans, and high confidence they are test-only and bounded per fixture.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact request-history size varies by fixture, but committed fixtures and per-test reset establish small bounded placeholder counts; no realistic severe test-throughput regression is evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds linear in-memory normalization work but no new remote boundary, concurrency burst, or product-path cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot CLI compacted shell-output persistence E2E
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new test creates a workspace, starts a real test session, runs node warnings.ts through the provider shell, waits for two replayed model turns, reads the preserved output through resourceRead, and asserts the result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/suites/copilotRuntimeToolsSuite.ts test runtime tools: compacted shell output preserves the complete original
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute node warnings.ts via the provider shell tool
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This E2E scenario and subprocess did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first model turn waits for command completion

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the original output through the Agent Host resourceRead protocol call
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one IPC call and underlying file read
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No read was performed because the test did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The assertion waits for the resource read

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Exchange deterministic model requests with the loopback replay proxy
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These two test exchanges did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each test turn waits for its replay response

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly 80 repeated warning lines, one shell invocation, one preserved output resource, two model turns, and one resource read per Copilot CLI parity-suite run.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The shell invocation, replayed model turns, resource read, and follow-up are deliberately serialized; no loop or aggregate burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The generated workspace and shell-output resource are cold and unique to the test. No cross-test cache is expected or defeated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the exact subprocess, IPC, and replay counts from the test and capture.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider startup duration varies by platform, but cardinality is fixed and the work is intentional coverage rather than a product workflow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This is bounded intentional E2E coverage, not repeated or scaling work added to a product path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Codex image attachment restoration after host restart
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new test creates one image attachment, completes a turn, restarts and initializes the host, restores the session, reads the attachment through resourceRead, and completes one follow-up turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restart the shared Agent Host/provider process
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one restart for this added test
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This added scenario did not perform a restart before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Restoration cannot proceed until restart and initialization finish

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the restored attachment through resourceRead
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one IPC call with one underlying file read
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No attachment read existed because the scenario was absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The final assertion waits for the read

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serve deterministic Codex model exchanges over the loopback replay proxy
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each turn waits for its replay response

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One 116-character base64 image payload, one attachment, one restart, one resource read, and two replayed model exchanges.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All steps are serial and awaited. No fan-out or burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The session and attachment are cold and unique; restart intentionally exercises persisted storage. There is no warm-cache path relevant to this one-shot test.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the exact serial boundaries from the test implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host restart time is platform-dependent, but all input and operation counts are fixed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added cost is fixed, intentional persistence-test coverage and does not alter product behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Codex invalid workspace-skill diagnostics and suite workspace cleanup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added test creates two invalid skill files, starts a session and one replayed turn, waits for customization notification, subscribes, stats the returned files, and asserts diagnostics. Workspace deletion now waits until the shared Codex process is disposed in suite teardown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the workspace and two SKILL.md files, then stat returned paths
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One workspace, two writes, and four small stat calls including expected and actual identities
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The test and these filesystem operations did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Creation precedes session startup; stats precede the final assertion

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serve one deterministic model exchange through the loopback replay proxy
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No exchange existed for this absent test.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The test waits for turn completion

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delete Codex-specific temporary workspaces after server disposal
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cleanup call for two currently registered directories
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same directories were deleted after each test; the diff moves deletion after shared-process disposal to release Windows watchers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only suite teardown waits; test turns are complete

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two skill files and one workspace for the new test, plus one existing multi-root temporary parent retained until teardown; current retained directory cardinality is two.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: File creation, model turn, notification, subscription, and stat calls are serial. Suite teardown disposes the server before one batched removeTempDirs call.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Skill discovery uses a fresh workspace, so it is cold by design. No cache key or negative-cache behavior is changed in product code.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in cleanup ownership and current retained cardinality from all tempDirs.push sites in the suite.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Future test additions could increase retained temporary directories, but current cardinality is two small trees and no unbounded production lifetime exists.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Cleanup is delayed by design until watcher ownership ends, with bounded tiny retention and one teardown deletion.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing worktree turn completes, the strengthened test scans received notifications, subscribes to the session, lists sessions, and synchronously asks git for the materialized branch before assertions and subsequent shell verification.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to the session and list the root session catalog
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two protocol calls per worktree test, independent of catalog item count except response serialization
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The test already subscribed earlier but did not issue these post-turn snapshot/catalog calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both calls complete before assertions and later shell verification

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run git branch --show-current in the resolved worktree
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one git subprocess per provider execution
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No post-turn git subprocess was used for the branch assertion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronously blocks only this E2E test before assertions

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One session, one catalog lookup, one subscribe call, one listSessions call, and one git branch subprocess per provider execution of this worktree test.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two protocol calls and git subprocess are serial after the model turn; no per-session or per-item fan-out occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Assertions read current authoritative session state and the materialized repository. No cache is introduced or bypassed; the added operations are one-shot.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the serial added boundaries and their one-shot cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Subprocess startup and catalog serialization vary by platform and suite state, but operation counts are fixed and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The bounded calls strengthen an E2E assertion and do not affect product runtime or scale with rows/events in a hot path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 14 changed files and every diff page. The PR adds bounded deterministic E2E scenarios, small replay-normalization scans, and delayed cleanup for two temporary directories. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not itself prove a shipped performance-regression fix.
